summary: The note is a feature article on ghostly processions said to appear on moonless nights in the rural town of Elders Hollow. It collects eyewitness accounts from 2023, a historical 1874 journal, a 1922 photograph and a parapsychologist's inconclusive investigation, alongside the sheriff's skepticism. It presents the legend as a shared heritage that ties the community to its past.
one_line: Feature on Elders Hollow's moonless-night ghost processions, covering 2023 eyewitnesses, historical records, a paranormal investigation, and the legend's role in community identity.
key_facts: Retired schoolteacher Agnes Bennett claimed to have first seen the ghostly procession on 13 September 2023, describing silent apparitions in antiquated garb passing through the copse at the edge of her property.
Young farmer Elias Harper corroborated Agnes Bennett's account weeks later, describing ghostly figures carrying lanterns that cast no light and wandered the same path through his fields.

Town archivist Meredith Green provided a tattered journal from 1874 written by Ezekiel Foster, a founding figure of the community, describing "a solemn company of spirits" near the fledgling settlement.
Ezekiel Foster, rooted in the spiritualism of his time, regarded the visitations as omens of change and documented them in his ledger.

At an Elders Hollow Historical Society meeting on September 29, 2023, octogenarian Walter Jennings presented a black-and-white photograph he said his grandfather took of the ghosts on a dark night in fall 1922; the claim met skepticism and awe.
On October 17, 2023, parapsychologist Dr. Lisa Moreno investigated with equipment for detecting electromagnetic anomalies and inaudible audio frequencies; her findings were inconclusive.
Dr. Lisa Moreno said the atmosphere in Elders Hollow on moonless nights is "undeniably charged with an otherworldly energy."
Sheriff Thomas Keller regards the stories as harmless folklore, but his team patrols on moonless nights over concerns about pranksters; they have made no arrests and have not dispelled the sightings.
Amateur historian Emily Martin said at the folklore enthusiasts club gathering on November 2, 2023: "These tales tell us more about ourselves than about the ghosts."
Mechanic Jonah Briggs, whose truck broke down near the crossroads by the old silo in September 2023, heard footsteps from an invisible group growing louder, though the night air was still and warm.

In October 2023, high school students Layla Thompson and Reuben Clarke went out for a social media challenge; Layla's phone shut down while recording and they heard the muffled beating of a drum before fleeing.
